critical_code_review_comments: realtime_core.py: _run_agent_engine catches all Exceptions and falls through to plain LLM reply for viewer_question auto-detect (good UX). But there's a duplicated `if action in (viewer_question, question, cli_message)` block — the second block ALWAYS runs after a successful auto-detect run_engine because the first only returns on success, and on exception it falls through to LLM reply. That's OK behavior but the code is a bit tangled; refactor for clarity.

server.py /paypal/orders: In LIVE mode this endpoint will actually create real PayPal orders against Frasberg's merchant account for any authenticated user request. Consider rate-limiting or a nonce/CSRF check to prevent abuse (an attacker with a valid session could spam order creation, which may cost API quota and trigger PayPal risk flags).

server.py /keys/usage/daily: aggregates 3000 usage docs per call with no cache; a user with many keys and heavy traffic could slow the endpoint. Consider a small (30-60s) TTL cache or pre-aggregated daily rollup collection.

Frontend LinqBilling: PayPal buttons render 3 SDK containers (linq-operator/architect/sovereign). Ensure the SDK is loaded once and buttons are re-rendered/cleaned up on tab switch to avoid duplicate iframes on remount.

run_engine artifact stored in linq_events with the LIVE room artifact 'lite' dict — good (no ObjectId). Confirmed 'engine' field is present so the frontend engine-artifact-{threat|billing|compliance} selector should key off it.
No rate limiting on /agents/luchii/actions run_engine — each call triggers an AI generation (5-30s). Authenticated abuse possible; consider per-user throttle.
